claims.text: Optimizing the laser scanning strategy improves dimensional precision in additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
Optimizing the laser scanning strategy improves mechanical integrity in additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
Optimizing the laser scanning strategy reduces fabrication-induced defects in additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
The high-entropy alloy begins in powder form.
An optimized laser scanning strategy modifies the resulting microstructure and porosity.
An optimized laser scanning strategy reduces thermal gradients during additive manufacturing.
An optimized laser scanning strategy reduces residual stresses in the manufactured component.
The intervention produces more than a 5% improvement in dimensional precision relative to the conventional fabrication baseline.
The intervention produces more than a 10% improvement in mechanical integrity relative to the conventional fabrication baseline.
Fabrication-induced defects are below 20% under the optimized strategy relative to the current fabrication baseline.
The proposed effect applies under controlled-atmosphere and controlled-temperature additive-manufacturing conditions.
The current fabrication baseline is a conventional additive-manufacturing process without an optimized laser scanning strategy.
The hypothesis is limited to particular high-entropy-alloy compositions and additive-manufacturing processes.
